The case is Boulus Constructions Pty Ltd v Warrumbungle Shire Council (No 2) [2022] NSWSC 1368.
The hearing dates for the case are 30 September 2022 and further written submissions on 5 October 2022.
The date of orders in the case is 12 October 2022.
The decision date in the case is 12 October 2022.
The jurisdiction of the case is Equity - Technology and Construction List.
The judge in the case is Stevenson J.
The Builder is Boulus Constructions Pty Limited.
The Builder is constructing a retirement village known as the Three Rivers Regional Retirement Community.
The retirement village is being constructed on a former hospital site in Dunedoo.
The Builder commenced the proceedings on 6 November 2018.
The Builder seeks to be paid what it asserts is due for the construction work.
The Council has brought a Cross-Claim alleging defective works.
The Council alleges some 300 defects in total in the retirement village.
The defects comprise some 30 different kinds of defect in multiple locations in the units within the retirement village.
A complex range of factual, legal and procedural issues has arisen in the case.
The matter was set down for a hearing to take place in July of last year, but that hearing was vacated.
There is no current hearing date for the case.
On 20 April 2022, the Builder served a Second Further Amended Technology and Construction List Statement and a Third Further Amended Technology and Construction Cross-Claim List Response.
The Builder alleges that the Council is not entitled to any remedy for the allegedly defective works due to the failure to obtain a valid Development Consent and Construction Certificate.
The Builder had made allegations regarding the lack of a valid Development Consent and Construction Certificate in earlier iterations of its List Statement.
Mr Feller SC appeared with Mr Marshall for the Council.
Mr Feller accepted that if the Builder makes out its allegation regarding the lack of a valid Development Consent and Construction Certificate, the Council may fail in its defective work claim.

The Council seeks to amend its Cross-Claim Cross-Summons and Cross-Claim List Statement to include a claim under s 37 of the Design and Building Practitioners Act 2020 (NSW) against the Builder and against Mr Brian Boulus and Mr Bradley McCarthy.
Mr Boulus and Mr McCarthy are not presently cross-defendants.
Section 37 of the Act provides a duty of care to avoid economic loss caused by defects in or related to a building for which construction work is done.
The duty of care is owed to each owner of the land in relation to which the construction work is carried out and to each subsequent owner of the land.
The duty of care is owed to an owner whether or not the construction work was carried out under a contract or other arrangement.
Sections 36 and 37 of the Act commenced operation on 10 June 2020 and have retrospective effect.
